items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: the teacher that I had was an old Italian fellow that if you made mistakes he would hit you on his fingers with a ruler or something

ctx.x: Well, I know, it all started when you saw your first what —

No, no, my first instrument was clarinet. I had a uncle that lived — my younger uncle who was about ten years older than I am, took clarinet lessons and he was very bad. But he used to leave his clarinet up on the mantelpiece and then he would go out and play. And I used to sit and watch him. So I would just take his clarinet and play it. So in other words I figured out how he fingered and what it was supposed to sound like, so I figured out all the notes, and that was it. So my grandfather happened to come in…
